narrative: The model estimated a 17% probability that you will fail your final year. While this is below half, it is still a meaningful risk that has led to the requirement for remedial courses. The three most influential factors in this assessment were your past class failures, your desire for higher education, and your mother’s occupation. Notably, all three pushed toward passing: you have zero past failures (matching the average of students who passed), you want to pursue higher education (as do all passing students), and your mother works as a teacher (20.7% of passers share this). These are protective strengths. However, other factors raised your overall risk to 17%. Your school absences are 8, compared to an average of 3.78 among passers, and your weekly study time is under 2 hours, while most passers study 2–5 hours. Your weekend alcohol consumption is high, whereas most passers report very low or low consumption. To improve your academic performance, focus on attending school more consistently, increasing your study time to at least 2–5 hours per week, and moderating weekend drinking. These changes can build on your existing strengths and lower your risk further.
